clue.text: Vehicle owner after crashing is showing signs of stress

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: something that has been in a crash is mangled, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A driver looks shaken after a car accident.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the owner a shaken driver, but 'after crashing' only mixes up the letters of 'owner', which then follow the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone worn down by worry and care visibly shows strain.

clue.text: In favour of exercises before runs? Correct

indicators.note: says the exercises come ahead of the runs in the answer

parts.note: to be pro something is to be in favour of it
PE, physical education, is school exercises
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A fitness fan asks whether the right routine is to exercise before going for a run.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper and correct are synonyms for doing things in the right way.

clue.text: Badge of soldier coming back inside inn as I ordered

indicators.note: places the turned soldier within the rearranged letters
the words inn as I are put into a different order here
means the letters for the soldier are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A returning soldier's badge is spotted in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The American soldier is a crossword regular. 'ordered' makes INSNIA from 'inn as I', and the soldier, 'coming back', goes 'inside' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignia are emblems or badges showing rank or membership.

clue.text: I must consume starter of cheese no longer

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter, here from cheese

explanation.surface: Someone is told they must eat a cheese course.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, describing what is no longer the case.

clue.text: Bread reportedly for female animal

indicators.note: means as it is said out loud, so the slang word is matched by its sound

parts.note: dough is slang for money, i.e. bread

explanation.surface: A baker's question about which bread suits an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A doe is the female of deer, rabbits and similar animals.

clue.text: Take out US weekly to do something whilst waiting

parts.note: to take out someone is slang for kill
Time is an American weekly news magazine

explanation.surface: Someone takes out a US magazine to read during a wait.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means passing idle time with some occupation until something happens.

clue.text: Measure rodent against porcupine's tail

indicators.note: places one piece next to the other

parts.note: a rat is a rodent

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter, here from porcupine's

explanation.surface: Comparing a rodent with a porcupine's spiny tail.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to assess or measure its worth.

clue.text: Help to cross river, dried up?

indicators.note: the helping word straddles the river, so the river letter goes inside it

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: Someone helps a traveller across a river that has run dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid land is parched and dry.

clue.text: Feathered friend? Emu's OTT, I fancy

indicators.note: fancy as a verb hints at imaginative rearrangement, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher thinks an emu is over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT means 'over the top'. The question mark signals the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A titmouse is a small songbird, a feathered friend in jokey terms.

clue.text: Be indebted to the openers in our Warwickshire eleven

indicators.note: openers start the innings, so take the starting letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: A cricket fan feels grateful to their county team's opening batsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: Warwickshire is an English county with a first-class cricket team; openers are the first batsmen in.
explanation.definitionFit: To owe is to be in debt to someone.

clue.text: What one eats in this assembly?

definitions.meaning: the food a person habitually consumes
a formal legislative assembly, as in some European parliaments

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both one's habitual food and a legislative gathering such as the Japanese parliament.

clue.text: Right one developing gun

parts.note: something that evolves is an evolver, one that develops

explanation.surface: A firearm designer's right-hand prototype taking shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' looks like an anagram signal, but 'one developing' is a single description.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolver is a handgun with a rotating cylinder.

clue.text: Note decorative additions round university's central hall

parts.note: A is a musical note

indicators.note: the trim goes around the letter for university

parts.note: trim is ornamental edging added to clothes or furniture

explanation.surface: Someone notes the ornaments around a college's main hall.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is a central open court or hall in a building.

clue.text: Start factory, almost without dividing walls

parts.note: to open a business is to start it

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its final letter goes

parts.note: a plant is a factory

explanation.surface: Launching a factory before its interior walls are finished.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-plan layout has few or no internal partitions.

clue.text: Promenade that is close to our border

parts.note: the front is the seaside promenade
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, here from our

explanation.surface: A seaside promenade runs right up to the national border.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontier is the boundary line between countries.

clue.text: A fruit skin said to be attractive

indicators.note: means as it is spoken, so the phrase is matched by a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a peel, the skin of a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone claims a fruit's skin is the attractive part.
explanation.definitionFit: To appeal is to be pleasing or attractive to someone.

clue.text: Constant tease in bed

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
to rib someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: Someone keeps teasing a partner in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A crib is a baby's cot, a small bed.

clue.text: Hotel guest trendies disturbed

indicators.note: letters that are disturbed are shaken out of order, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hotel guest is disturbed by noisy fashionable types.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident is someone staying at a hotel, as opposed to a casual visitor.

clue.text: Have a bet about northern composer

indicators.note: the betting word wraps around the letter for northern

parts.note: to wager is to have a bet

explanation.surface: Someone bets on a composer from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Wagner was a German composer of operas such as the Ring cycle.

clue.text: Check about home

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Checking up on matters to do with the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in is to restrain or check, as with a horse.

clue.text: Refurbished tavern feeding the Italian for a spell

indicators.note: the rearranged pub goes into the Italian article

parts.note: il is Italian for the

indicators.note: a refurbished place is done over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A renovated pub serves an Italian for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' here is a period of time, not magic. 'Refurbished' makes NTERVA from the pub word, and 'feeding' puts that inside the Italian article.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval is a period of time, as is a spell.

clue.text: Salute FT, unexpectedly pleasing

indicators.note: something unexpected comes out differently, so these letters change order

explanation.surface: A reader surprised to approve of the Financial Times.
explanation.walkthrough: FT is the Financial Times newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasteful decor or design is in good taste and so agreeable.

clue.text: Humiliate act, blue

parts.note: to do is to act
feeling blue is feeling down

explanation.surface: Someone humiliated, acting depressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone down is to belittle or put them down.

clue.text: Instructs classes

definitions.meaning: commands or tells someone to do something
ranks or categories, as in holy ... or social ...

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both commands someone and ranks or categories of things.

clue.text: Assist male over record

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece sits over the other

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A man helps with a vinyl record.
explanation.definitionFit: To help and to assist are synonyms.

clue.text: Refuse to have Republican in bar

indicators.note: places the Republican letter inside the banning word

parts.note: to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: Declining to allow a Republican into a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun: waste husks.
explanation.definitionFit: Bran is the husk separated from grain, a waste by-product.
